analysis.title: US Rates Watch: Flows & positioning: short momentum loss
key_insights: Positioning and flows point to two-way risk in rates. Shorts continue to see momentum turn against them after another significant rally.
CTA short covering now faces the most risk at the front end. Those triggers are a key threshold for a rally extension.

Asset managers covered shorts and added longs in futures across the curve last week. The gap between front end/belly positioning and the long end narrowed slightly, a reprieve from strong steepener positioning over the last month.

The futures positioning proxy now implies a bias for rates to move lower across the curve, except TU (2Y). Longs retreated as shorts moved more out of the money. Shorts remain the more concentrated position.
The futures proxy suggests a bias for the curve to flatten. BofA's historical analysis calls this proxy a modest contrarian signal for duration and gives no clear signal for the curve.

As of Friday only front-end CTA shorts remain outside covering range. Belly and long-end CTA shorts rallied through their ranges the prior week, so front-end trigger ranges are within reach if the rally extends.

US fixed income fund inflows rebounded last week as investors rotated from duration to spread risk, mainly corporates. Flows moved from front-end Treasury funds to belly duration and IG and HY corporate funds.
Long-end Treasury funds remain out of favor. Agg-style allocation funds receive only about a third of their rolling 52-week average inflows.

Active funds cut duration overweights and became less underweight IG, signaling a return to spread products over duration. They stay modestly overweight MBS. Fund outperformance narrowed notably after the broad rate selloff.

In the week ending Oct 21, bank assets fell significantly (-$161bn) on drawdowns in domestic cash and other foreign assets. Domestic deposits fell $167bn. Domestic bank MBS holdings are even with July 2025 levels while UST and agency holdings keep rising.

Currency-hedged pickup of 10Y USTs is negative versus 10Y JGBs, 20Y JGBs, CAD and gilts, and slightly positive versus Bunds. For Japanese investors the 10Y UST pickup is -0.97% versus 10Y JGBs and -1.80% versus 20Y JGBs (Oct 22).

Foreign flows: Canada was the largest buyer of USTs and Japan and China the largest sellers in the latest TIC month. Foreign participation at auctions has fallen back below 20%. Dealer participation remains low and investment fund participation remains elevated.
Japanese investors' foreign bond flows in September showed pension buying (+$7.6bn) and bank selling (-$15.8bn), consistent with prior months.

Flow of funds data shows household UST demand grew in 2Q26, likely driven largely by hedge funds. Hedge fund cash UST holdings have grown since 2022 and leveraged fund short futures are back to Q2 2025 levels.

Pension data: UST stripping activity was nearly non-existent in August despite elevated yields. Pension funded status has historically improved as rates rise, and funds with higher funded status buy more USTs.
Week-ahead calendar includes ISM Manufacturing (BofA 53.9 vs consensus 54.7), ISM Services (54.8 vs 54.8) and payrolls on Nov 6 (BofA +75k vs consensus +65k).

risk_factors: Front-end CTA short covering could extend the rally if trigger ranges are hit.
Two-way risk in rates as shorts face momentum headwinds but the futures proxy is contrarian.
Foreign demand for USTs is weak on a hedged basis, and auction foreign participation has fallen below 20%.
Large weekly drops in bank deposits and cash could affect bank demand for securities.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 plots the 2y and 5y rate levels against CTA buy trigger ranges, on a 4.50-4.75% axis. Only front-end CTA shorts remain outside covering range.
vol_and_positioning: BofA's Curve-o-meter says rates should trade as if positioning is modestly short and in a steepener.
Futures proxy and CTA positioning skew short on duration, while fund regression skews long. CTA positioning and the futures proxy skew toward steepeners.
In the futures proxy, shorts continue to move out of the money as longs retreat. Futures proxy implies the curve rallies except at the front end.
CTA 10Y beta rose modestly on the week. Non-reportable positions and betas both suggest a recent increase in shorts.

Historically the futures proxy is a modest contrarian signal for duration (short positioning precedes rate declines). Fund regression and CFTC asset manager duration signals follow trends. CTA betas show no strong signal.
Asset manager longs correspond with leveraged fund shorts. Asset managers have a significant long-end decline since September.
Primary dealers cut holdings notably at the long end across cash and futures over the week. Belly futures and long-end UST holdings are down meaningfully over six months.

tension_points.bull_case: Shorts face momentum headwinds, the futures positioning proxy is biased for rates to fall across the curve except TU, and front-end CTA shorts are close to covering, which could extend the rally.
tension_points.bear_case: Funds are rotating from duration to spread products, foreign hedged demand for USTs is weak, and the curve-o-meter says rates trade as if positioning is modestly short, so risk remains two-way.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Front-end CTA buy trigger ranges (about 4.50-4.75% on the 2y and 5y) are not reached, so shorts are not forced to cover.
